title: Maya and the Sleepy Star
pages: Once upon a time, in a cosy house at the end of a quiet lane, lived a girl called Maya. Maya loved three things more than almost anything: rockets, the moon, and her fluffy dog, Biscuit.
One evening, as the sky turned the colour of blueberry jam, Maya pressed her nose to the window. High above the rooftops, one little star was blinking very slowly, as if it was trying to stay awake.
"Biscuit," whispered Maya, "I think that star is tired." Biscuit wagged his tail and gave a soft little woof, which Maya knew meant, "Let's help."
So Maya built a rocket from her duvet, two pillows and a cardboard box. She drew buttons with her favourite crayons and gave Biscuit a special co-pilot's hat. "Three, two, one… lift off!"
Up, up they floated, past the chimney pots and the sleeping birds, until the whole town looked like a twinkly blanket below them. The moon smiled a big silver smile and said, "Hello, Maya."
The little star was curled up on a cloud. "I'm the newest star in the sky," it yawned, "and I don't know how to shine and rest at the same time." Maya thought very carefully, the way she always did.
"When I'm sleepy," said Maya kindly, "I take three slow breaths, like this." She breathed in… and out. In… and out. In… and out. The little star copied her, and began to glow a soft, warm gold.
"Thank you, Maya," whispered the star. "Now I can shine gently all night long." Biscuit gave the star a happy lick, and it giggled a twinkly giggle.
The rocket drifted slowly home, down past the sleeping birds and the chimney pots, and in through Maya's window. Her bed was warm and her pillow was soft.
Maya snuggled down with Biscuit curled at her feet. Outside, the little star shone gently, just for her. Maya took three slow breaths… in and out… and drifted off to sleep.
